findings.title: Adding an abstract SPI method breaks already deployed grant providers at startup
findings.body: Existing third-party OAuth2GrantTypeFactory implementations compiled against the previous interface do not implement getShortcut(). DefaultTokenContextEncoderProviderFactory.postInit() invokes this method for every registered grant factory, so an unchanged provider JAR causes AbstractMethodError during server initialization (and source-based providers no longer compile). Provide a compatible default/migration path or otherwise avoid making this new method abstract for existing provider implementations.

findings.title: The public OAuth2 grant context copy constructor was removed
findings.body: The previous public Context(Context) constructor was removed rather than updated to copy grantType. Custom grant providers can use this constructor to derive a context before invoking another grant flow; binaries compiled against the prior server SPI will fail with NoSuchMethodError when that path executes, and source users cannot compile. Restore the constructor and copy the new grantType field.

findings.title: Grant shortcuts are not constrained to the two-character token wire format
findings.body: This factory accepts and stores arbitrary getShortcut() values, but the encoder writes the shortcut directly into the ID while the decoder only accepts exactly six context characters and slices the grant field to two characters. A custom grant returning a three-character shortcut (which the OAuth2GrantTypeFactory documentation currently even describes as usual) will issue IDs such as onrtabc:<id> that this provider subsequently rejects as malformed. Validate that shortcuts are exactly two characters when registering factories, or change the format/parser to support variable-length shortcuts and document the contract consistently.

findings.title: rawTokenId is never null-checked
findings.body: The constructor checks grantType twice; the second check has the rawTokenId error message but still passes grantType. Consequently an AccessTokenContext with a null rawTokenId is accepted and encodeTokenId serializes it as the literal string "null", causing otherwise identical token contexts to share the same JTI. Check rawTokenId instead so invalid contexts fail before an invalid/non-unique token ID is generated.

findings.title: Access-token event matcher accepts IDs with the wrong grant shortcut
findings.body: isAccessTokenId extracts substring(3, 5), although the six-character prefix stores the grant at indexes 4..5, and it returns false when that incorrectly extracted value equals the expected shortcut. For example, onrtac:<uuid> is accepted for expected "ac" only because "ta" does not match. Thus the updated integration assertions do not verify the encoded grant type and can pass when the implementation emits an incorrect shortcut. Compare substring(4, 6) and reject non-matching values.
